candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — preventive care, screening, postpartum health-promotion activities.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — postpartum mental-health screening
candidate.educational_objective: Provide routine postpartum depression and anxiety screening with a standardized, validated instrument and ensure a system exists for timely assessment, treatment, monitoring, and follow-up.

options.A: Screen only when the client reports persistent sadness, loss of interest, or another symptom suggesting a postpartum mood disorder.
options.B: Omit postpartum screening if depression screening was already completed during pregnancy.
options.C: Refer all mood screening to a mental-health specialist rather than using validated tools in obstetric care.
options.D: Screen for depression and anxiety with a standardized, validated instrument and have systems for timely assessment and follow-up.

candidate.rationale: ACOG recommends that everyone receiving postpartum care be screened for depression and anxiety using standardized, validated instruments. Screening should be implemented with systems that ensure timely assessment and diagnosis, effective treatment, and appropriate monitoring and follow-up according to severity. Therefore D is correct even when the client does not volunteer symptoms or a psychiatric history.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Routine postpartum depression and anxiety screening is recommended for all patients using standardized validated instruments, with systems for timely assessment, treatment and follow-up.
